course_description:
How do you lead in an era where the only constant is change? This course moves beyond innovation as a one-off event, focusing instead on building a sustainable innovation culture as a core strategic capability. Through collaborative problem-solving and live innovation challenges, you will develop the practical skills to identify, build, and lead innovation capabilities within startups, SMEs, and large-scale organisations. You will emerge with the strategic mindset and employability skills sought by modern organisations looking to harness creativity and scale their innovative processes in dynamic environments.

In today's continuously changing business environment, innovation is essential for the long-term success of organisations. Yet, efforts to become more innovative often fail because many organisations are hostile environments for innovation. In this course you will learn new skills, capabilities and strategies that will help you identify and drive innovation in teams and organisations. You will develop skills in creating organisational cultures and structures that support innovation, build capacity and resources in teams and learn skills to become a leader who champions innovation.

EIBS7303 allows you to learn about the latest thinking and practices in innovation through real-world case challenges and collaborative simulation activities . Working in fast-paced, device-free environments, you will develop the agility to analyse dynamic industry sectors and pitch innovation strategies under realistic conditions. You will also take the role of consultants to analyse and write a comprehensive report on the strategic steps an organization can take to build an ongoing capability for innovation. Finally, students will construct a personal reflective portfolio that captures your individual learning journey to become a future innovation leader.

Sustainable Development Goals - UQ Business School is a proud supporter and Advanced Signatory of the United Nations Principles for Responsible Management Education (UN PRME) . As part of the largest global collaboration between business schools and the UN, the school emphasises its role in empowering students to drive societal transformation through the Sustainable Development Goals . The SDGs highlight that a thriving economy relies on a healthy environment, aiming to balance economic growth, social well-being, and environmental protection for a sustainable future.

course_aims: The central foundation for this course is the building of innovation capability of self, team, and organisation. This will be done using information, advice and feedback from a range of sources applied to a real case organisation and reflected in assessment that tracks your personal evolution in undertaking this scholarly inquiry.

learning_outcomes.description: Critique the foundations of innovation performance and the balance between flexibility and efficiency in dynamic environments.
Collaborate effectively within diverse teams to develop informed strategic innovation decisions.
Appraise the ethical implications and strategic risks associated with embedding innovation capabilities in modern organisations.
Construct a professional portfolio of personal attributes and skills to drive future innovation leadership.

assessment_details.task_description: This task is strictly secure and screen-free. This assessment comprises 5 graded components in total (5 x 8% = 40%): 4 team-based content scores (8% x 4 = 32%) derived from weekly activities between weeks 5 and 8, and 1 individual pitch score (8%). For each weekly activity, students will prepare by reviewing course content and a designated case study or sector. During the class session, students will be randomly assigned to teams of four to collaborate, apply the designated course content, and prepare a short pitch (3–5 minutes). To assess the ability to collaborate effectively within diverse groups, teams will be reshuffled randomly for each activity. Please Note: The presentation will be recorded for marking purposes per UQ Policy. Read full task description Hide full task description
assessment_details.assessment_security: Secure assessment: This assessment is designed to protect academic integrity and assess your understanding of course concepts. You must only use the approved materials and tools for this assessment task. Use of prohibited materials in this task may be investigated and treated as academic misconduct. See assessment instructions for more details.
assessment_details.submission_guidelines:
This is an in-class assessment. For each weekly activity (Weeks 5-8), students will collaborate in randomly assigned teams to prepare and deliver a short pitch during the class session. There is no individual file submission required on Blackboard for the weekly activities, as grading is completed based on in-class performance. Detailed instructions for the individual components will be provided on Blackboard.
Deferral or extension
You may be able to apply for an extension .
The maximum extension allowed is 14 days. Extensions are given in multiples of 24 hours.
As this assessment consists of live, in-class activities, standard extensions of time are not applicable. Students who experience illness or exceptional circumstances on the day of an activity must apply for an extension/alternative arrangement through the official UQ system with appropriate documentation. Approved students will be provided with an alternative task or adjustment as determined by the Course Coordinator.
Late submission
As this assessment consists of live, in-class activities and team-based pitches, late submissions cannot be accepted. Students who miss a session without an approved extension or alternative arrangement will receive a mark of zero for that week's component.
